title: On the day of the exam
subtitle: MFML comprehensive (EC-3) · 6 Dec 2026, morning · open book · 150 minutes · quick checks and rules collected while studying

lesson.title: Quick checks
lesson.lead: Short rules to apply on the paper. Each one says where it came from, so you can open the full solution.

blocks.text: ∇J = 0  ⇒  solve;   then  H positive definite (D₁ > 0, D₂ > 0, …)  ⇒  minimum
blocks.caption: Always set the gradient to zero and solve the equations; confirm with the Hessian's leading minors

blocks.text: Example: [Practice Paper Q4(c)](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/p-pp/worked/4): ∇J = (2w₀ + 3w₁ − 4, 3w₀ + 5w₁ − 7) = 0 ⇒ (−1, 2); H = [[2, 3], [3, 5]], D₁ = 2, D₂ = 1 ⇒ minimum.

blocks.label: Remember
blocks.text: **The first momentum step is the same as plain GD, and the difference only starts at step 2** (because v₀ = 0).

items: If the question writes a formula or mentions a velocity v, use exactly that, and copy it onto your answer sheet first.
No formula given: use vₜ₊₁ = βvₜ − η∇f(wₜ), wₜ₊₁ = wₜ + vₜ₊₁, v₀ = 0.

Find-β questions: use the slide form wₜ₊₁ = wₜ − η∇f(wₜ) + β(wₜ − wₜ₋₁), or the v-form with v₀ = 0 (write "assume v₀ = 0"). Both give the same answer; see [2023 Q1A, Method 1 and Method 2](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch11/f-momentum/5).

blocks.text: 4 · Check the sign before every number

blocks.label: Double-check signs
blocks.text: **While solving any numerical, check the sign in front of each number before you write it down.** One wrong sign carries through every step that follows, and you lose the marks for all of them.

items: Minus times minus: −η∇f with a negative gradient gives a **plus**. Example: −0.1 × (−2) = +0.2.
Brackets inside gradients: d/dw (w + 1)² = 2(w + 1), so at w = 0 it is **+2**, while d/dw (w − 1)² at w = 0 is **−2**.
Velocity: v is often negative, so wₜ + vₜ₊₁ means you **subtract**.
Squaring: (−0.46)² is positive, and so is (w − 1)² when w < 1.
Lagrange and KKT: copy the sign of each constraint term exactly as you set up L (+λg or −λg), and keep it the same everywhere.
Before moving to the next step, re-read the line you just wrote and check each sign against the line above it.

blocks.text: Recent papers: 6 questions, 40 marks, 150 minutes. That is about **25 minutes per question** and **3.75 minutes per mark**. Keep 15 minutes aside (5 at the start to read the paper and choose your order, 10 at the end to check signs and answers). That leaves 135 minutes, about **3.4 minutes per mark**.

items: Start with your strongest questions (momentum, GD steps, Lagrange). They are quick marks and build up spare time.
Stuck at about 1.5× the budget? Move on, leave space on the sheet, and come back later.
Open book only helps if you know where things are. Mark the formula pages beforehand so you don't lose minutes searching.

blocks.text: w₀ = given starting point;   v₀ = (0, 0) unless the question gives it
blocks.caption: Write "assume v₀ = 0" as the first line of the answer

items: w₀ (where you start) and v₀ (how fast you were already moving) are separate. Being given w₀ does not change v₀.
No step has been taken before the start, so nothing has built up yet: v₀ = 0. The first step is then the same as plain GD.
Use a non-zero v₀ only when the question gives one, or gives two starting points (w₋₁ and w₀).
**✓ Approved by Saurabh sir:** he confirmed v₀ = (0, 0) for [2023 Q1A (find β)](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch11/f-momentum/5).

blocks.text: 7 · GD step size: monotone, oscillating or divergent
xₜ₊₁ = (1 − αλ) xₜ,  λ = f″:   α < 1/λ monotone;   1/λ < α < 2/λ oscillating;   α > 2/λ divergent
blocks.caption: For f = x² (λ = 2): cut-offs α = 0.5 and α = 1

items: Find r from the data: divide each x by the one before it. The same r every time means plain GD.
Then α = (1 − r)/λ (for f = x²: α = (1 − r)/2).
0 < r < 1: same side, shrinking (monotone). −1 < r < 0: sign flips, shrinking (oscillating). r < −1: sign flips, growing (divergent).
Example: [Sourabh Optimizers Set Q7(a)](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch11/f-momentum/22). Runs A, B, C give r = 0.8, −0.5, −1.2, so α = 0.1, 0.75, 1.1.
Background and the full recipe (four question types): [Lecture 9 · Step-size behaviour](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch09/lesson/9).

blocks.text: 8 · Directional derivative: make the direction unit length

blocks.caption: d is a direction (an arrow), not a second point

items: Find ∇f at the point, then ‖d‖ = √(sum of squares), then u = d/‖d‖, then the dot product.
Skip dividing and the answer is ‖d‖ times too big. Example: d = (3, 4), ‖d‖ = 5, ∇f = (8, 0) gives 4.8, not 24.
Already length 1 (e.g. (0.6, 0.8), (1/√2, 1/√2))? Use it as it is.
Example: [Convexity · Sourabh P24 (c)](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch11/f-convex/4).

blocks.label: Keep adding
blocks.text: New rules go at the end of this board as they come up while studying.

formulas.name: Finding a minimiser
formulas.formula: ∇J = 0, solve; then H positive definite (leading minors > 0) ⇒ minimum

formulas.name: Momentum, first step
formulas.formula: v₁ = −η∇f(w₀) ⇒ w₁ = w₀ − η∇f(w₀) (same as plain GD)

formulas.name: Momentum update
formulas.formula: vₜ₊₁ = βvₜ − η∇f(wₜ),  wₜ₊₁ = wₜ + vₜ₊₁,  v₀ = 0
formulas.note: Use the question's own form if it gives one

formulas.name: Double-check signs
formulas.formula: Check the sign before every number: −η × (−g) = +ηg;  w + v with v < 0 means subtract
formulas.note: One wrong sign breaks every later step

formulas.name: Time per question
formulas.formula: 150 min, 40 marks, 6 questions ⇒ ~25 min per question; keep 15 min aside ⇒ ~3.4 min per mark (4 m ≈ 14 min, 6 m ≈ 20, 7 m ≈ 24, 8 m ≈ 27)
formulas.note: Stuck at 1.5× the budget? Move on and come back

formulas.name: Momentum, starting velocity
formulas.formula: v₀ = (0, 0) unless given; w₀ is the starting point (a different thing)
formulas.note: Write "assume v₀ = 0" · ✓ confirmed by Saurabh sir (2023 Q1A)

formulas.name: GD step-size behaviour
formulas.formula: r = 1 − αλ (λ = f″): α < 1/λ monotone; 1/λ < α < 2/λ oscillating; α > 2/λ divergent
formulas.note: f = x²: cut-offs 0.5 and 1 · α = (1 − r)/2

formulas.name: Directional derivative
formulas.formula: D_u f = ∇f · u,  u = d/‖d‖ (unit length first)
formulas.note: d = (3, 4) ⇒ u = (3/5, 4/5); skipping it gives 5× too big
